name: python-expedia-hotel-booking-searches
what_it_holds: Analysis of the classic Kaggle "Expedia Hotel Recommendations" competition search-log dataset (user aggregate purchase history and hotel prices vs. nights-stay outcomes, fields like srch_saturday_night_bool). This is search-intent/click data from ~2013-2014, not company-level KPI data.
why_useful: Marginal: it is old, user-level search-log data rather than an OTA volume/KPI series, but the underlying Kaggle dataset (Expedia, 37M+ rows) is a genuine large historical travel-search dataset that in principle could be mined for seasonality/demand patterns as a very rough competitor-OTA demand proxy.
size_hint: Kaggle source dataset is tens of millions of rows
themes: Company KPI and alt-data backtest repos for ABNB or OTAs: anyone who already assembled Airbnb quarterly KPI datasets, consensus, or alt-data panels

name: ilyankou/passport-index-dataset
what_it_holds: 313-star, actively maintained (updated 29 Aug 2026) repo with CSVs of visa requirements for 199 countries, 2019-2025 vintages, MIT licensed. Includes a passport-index-matrix.csv (bilateral visa-requirement matrix: visa-free / visa-on-arrival / e-visa / visa-required codes between every pair of countries) and passport-index-tidy.csv, refreshed periodically from the Passport Index / Henley-style source.
why_useful: A time-stamped, versioned visa-requirement matrix lets you build a cross-border 'ease of travel' index by origin country, useful as a slow-moving control variable for APAC/LatAm inbound demand shifts (gap #7) and as a covariate in any cross-border share model (gap #20); MIT license and multi-year vintages (2019-2025) make it usable point-in-time if commit history is walked.
size_hint: multiple CSVs, low MB, 199x199 country matrix per year
themes: Cross-border and visa data: Schengen visa statistics, ESTA, ETIAS, CBP wait times, passport index, border crossings BTS

why_all: A time-stamped, versioned visa-requirement matrix lets you build a cross-border 'ease of travel' index by origin country, useful as a slow-moving control variable for APAC/LatAm inbound demand shifts (gap #7) and as a covariate in any cross-border share model (gap #20); MIT license and multi-year vintages (2019-2025) make it usable point-in-time if commit history is walked.

A time-stamped (near point-in-time, annual snapshots 2019-2025) global visa-policy panel is exactly the "visa changes" shock category in the brief -- lets the team flag bilateral visa-requirement changes (e.g., a source country gaining/losing visa-free access to a destination) that would shift cross-border nights and regional mix, and is structured for a difference-in-differences design around policy-change dates.

name: EliseoCab/brownsville-wait-times
what_it_holds: Very fresh repo (last push 14 Sep 2026, same day as this scout) with committed XML snapshots of CBP Brownsville, TX Port of Entry wait times: data/bwt-all.xml (181KB, appears to be an accumulating historical log) and data/bwt.xml (3.3KB, latest snapshot), pulled from the public CBP Border Wait Times feed (bwt.cbp.gov).
why_useful: A single-port but actually time-stamped, accumulating CBP wait-time archive -- if bwt-all.xml is a running log it could give a real point-in-time series of land-border congestion (US-Mexico), a genuine proxy for cross-border travel volume (gap #10); worth checking XML contents/date range before relying on it, single port limits usefulness for a national picture.
time_coverage: unclear -- appears to be actively growing as of Sep 2026
